title: Remove legacy traffic-router endpoint and flatten config versioning
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Goal: Remove the long-lived /v0/traffic-router endpoint and the associated compatibility shim in the API gateway, and consolidate config versioning so that runtime config blobs are pinned to a single canonical version. This reduces complexity in routing logic, eliminates an extra code-path for KV cache warmup, and shrinks the surface area for feature flag shims that frequently regress when we change rollout rules.

Scope: API gateway endpoint removal, delete compatibility middleware, migrate existing routes using legacy configVersion fields to the new 'config_revision' canonical field, update migration tooling, update docs and client SDKs where necessary. Does NOT include removing user-facing rollout UI; that is tracked under PM backlog.

Success criteria:
- No requests are routed through /v0/traffic-router in production for 14 days during the canary window.
- All internal services report zero use of legacy configVersion within runtime-1.22 deploys.
- No performance regression in p50/p95 latency after removal (target: <1% change) and CPU tail unchanged.
- Automated migration completed for all existing deployment manifests in customer-dedicated pools.

Constraints and risks:
- Several legacy Dedicated customers still use older deployment manifests that rely on configVersion semantics; require migration or targeted exclusion.
- Rollback complexity if a dependent service continues to emit legacy headers.
- Security review required because this touches auth header parsing in the gateway.
updates: 2026-02-10: Spike completed to enumerate usages of /v0/traffic-router across services. Found 17 internal callers and 3 external partners (support tickets opened).
2026-02-17: Migration tool prototype (scripts/migrate-config-version) landed in GH draft PR #5128, initial smoke conversion of 50 manifests succeeded in staging.
2026-02-26: Decided to keep a short-lived compatibility flag 'compat.traffic_router.enabled' gated by org id for Dedicated customers. Plan to remove flag after 30-day org-level deprecation notices.
2026-03-03: Load test with gateway-v2 (no shim) passed 95th-percentile latency targets in perf lab (p95 +0.4%), CPU stable. Added perf regression test to CI.
2026-03-06: Security review kickoff with S&Sec; identified required audit logging changes for auth header parsing; ticket ENG-17510 opened for logging changes.
2026-03-12: Canary rollout to 10% of production traffic started. Observability dashboard (links below) shows no 500 spikes. Continuing monitoring for 7 more days.
qa_plan: Unit tests for gateway parser updated. Integration tests in staging convert 100% of manifests and run end-to-end smoke (generation, cache warmup, streaming). Performance lab run with synthetic production mix and 2x burst to validate no latency regression. Manual acceptance: run through dedicated customer smoke script and confirm KV cache hit behavior. Post-canary health checks automated for 14 days.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy migration scripts to tools-runner and convert non-exempt manifests in staging.
2) Deploy gateway with shim disabled behind org-gated 'compat.traffic_router.enabled' flag. Enable for 10% org traffic for 72 hours.
3) If stable, expand to 50% traffic for 7 days and target Dedicated customers for manual migration windows.
4) Final removal: flip off compat flag for all orgs and remove the shim from gateway, then prune configVersion code paths in runtime-1.22.
5) Post-removal: run full integration and perf sweep and close the deprecation announcement loop to customers.
rollback_plan: If we observe increased 500s or p95 latency regressions >2% or dedicated-customer failures, immediately re-enable the compat.traffic_router.enabled flag for all orgs and roll back gateway to prior stable image. Hold on final removal until affected orgs are migrated. Incident runbook updated with responsible on-call names.
notes: We intentionally did not fold this work into 'remove-old-flags' monolith because traffic-router touches auth parsing and dedicated customer migration workflows that require separate communication.
Customer communication plan: Security/PD will send org-scoped notices with migration steps and dedicated windows. Engineering to provide migration support for 2 weeks post-removal.
Follow-up: schedule a separate ticket to remove legacy rollout policy API endpoints used by internal rollout tooling after this removal is complete.
